title_en: Beijing Second Branch Procuratorate v. Cheng Shaozhi — bribery case
keywords_en: criminal; bribery; first instance; intermediate people's court; Beijing; natural person; state organ; criminal law; Whether acceptance of a bank card without actual withdrawal constitutes bribery; determination of subjective intent for bribery crime; support for plaintiff; bank card; bidding
full_text_en:
Cheng Shaozhi bribery case

[Ruling Summary]

A state functionary who, by taking advantage of his position, seeks benefits for others and accepts a bank card from others with an altered password shall be deemed to have completed the act of accepting money if he subjectively has an obvious intention of illegal possession, even though he has not actually withdrawn the deposit in the card at the time the case is uncovered. This constitutes the crime of bribery.

Procuratorial Authority: Beijing No. 2 Branch, People's Procuratorate.

Defendant: Cheng Shaozhi, male, 59 years old, formerly Deputy Director of the Oilfield Exploration and Development Management Department of China Petroleum & Chemical Corporation, residing in Chaoyang District, Beijing. Arrested on July 12, 2001.

The case of Cheng Shaozhi for bribery was instituted before the Beijing No. 2 Intermediate People's Court by the Beijing No. 2 Branch, People's Procuratorate, on February 21, 2002.

Allegations in the Indictment: Between 1997 and 1998, the defendant Cheng Shaozhi, during his tenure as Deputy Director of Henan Petroleum Exploration Bureau and later as Deputy Director of the Oilfield Exploration and Development Management Department of China Petroleum & Chemical Corporation, took advantage of his position to seek benefits on multiple occasions for Chen Hanshun, the agent of Allied Colloids (UK) Limited (hereinafter "Allied Colloids UK"), and for China International Enterprise Cooperation Corporation, in the tendering and bidding activities for the import of polyacrylamide. He accepted from Chen Hanshun a China Merchants Bank "All-in-One Card" containing 81,867 US dollars (equivalent to RMB 678,847.79). Cheng Shaozhi also, during his tenure as Deputy Director of Henan Petroleum Exploration Bureau and as head of the bidding team for the procurement of polyacrylamide, took advantage of his position to arrange for Ying Xinhai, a business person from Shanghai Sanqi Industrial Co., Ltd., to act as the intermediary agent for the business activities between Japan International Oil Co., Ltd. and Henan Petroleum Exploration Bureau, thereby seeking benefits for Ying Xinhai, and accepted USD 32,000 (equivalent to RMB 265,260.80) from Ying Xinhai. As a state functionary, Cheng Shaozhi, by taking advantage of his position to seek benefits for others and accepting property, has committed the crime of bribery. The amount of bribery is particularly huge, and punishment according to law is requested.

Defendant's Plea: Cheng Shaozhi argued that he accepted the China Merchants Bank "All-in-One Card" from Chen Hanshun for the purpose of helping him purchase overseas stocks; and that he did not accept the US dollars from Ying Xinhai.

Defense Counsel's Arguments: The defense argued that the allegation of Cheng Shaozhi accepting bribes from Chen Hanshun was not established. The purpose of the "All-in-One Card" was for Chen Hanshun to entrust Cheng Shaozhi to buy stocks. The US dollars in the "All-in-One Card" were in a time deposit, and Cheng Shaozhi could not directly withdraw them; therefore, the ownership of the deposit had not been transferred. The defense further argued that the evidence for the allegation of Cheng Shaozhi accepting bribes from Ying Xinhai was insufficient and could not be established.

Facts Found by the Beijing No. 2 Intermediate People's Court:

I. Between 1997 and June 1998, Cheng Shaozhi served as Deputy Director of Henan Petroleum Exploration Bureau and concurrently as head of the bidding team for the procurement and extraction of polyacrylamide. In the tendering activities for the import of polyacrylamide by Henan Petroleum Exploration Bureau, the 1285 polymer produced by Allied Colloids UK, represented by China International Enterprise Cooperation Corporation, won the bid. On May 2, 1997, and April 18, 1998, China International Enterprise Cooperation Corporation signed sales contracts for polyacrylamide with Henan Petroleum Exploration Bureau. In August 2000, the parties negotiated and amended the unit price and total price of polyacrylamide 1285HN produced by Allied Colloids UK in the contract (Contract No. 98CIECCO40520). On August 4 of the same year, Chen Hanshun (separately dealt with), the agent of Allied Colloids UK, to thank Cheng Shaozhi for his cooperation in the business activities, gave Cheng Shaozhi a China Merchants Bank "All-in-One Card" containing USD 81,867. The card account number was 001007090266, the deposit type was a lump-sum time deposit for a two-year term, equivalent to RMB 678,841.16. Also given was a slip of paper with the bank card password and the amount. Thereafter, Cheng Shaozhi changed the password and stored the bank card and the slip in a safe deposit box he had rented at the Yayuncun Sub-branch of China Merchants Bank, Beijing. The items were seized after the case was uncovered.

Main Evidence to Support the Above Facts:

1.  Reporting materials on the polymer bidding and ordering of Henan Petroleum Exploration Bureau. This proved that Cheng Shaozhi was the head of the bidding team for the procurement of polyacrylamide polymer for Henan Petroleum Exploration Bureau and the circumstances of the polymer bidding and winning.
2.  Text of the Industrial and Mineral Products Sales Contract (Contract No. 97Z160502). This proved the circumstances of the sales contract for polyacrylamide signed between China International Enterprise Cooperation Corporation and Henan Petroleum Exploration Bureau on May 2, 1997.
3.  Text of the Industrial and Mineral Products Sales Contract (Contract No. 98CIECCO40520). This proved the circumstances of the sales contract for polyacrylamide signed between China International Enterprise Cooperation Corporation and Henan Petroleum Exploration Bureau on April 18, 1998.
4.  Agreement on the amendment of Contract No. 98CIECCO40520. This proved the circumstances under which China International Enterprise Cooperation Corporation and Henan Petroleum Exploration Bureau, through negotiation, amended the supply unit price, total price, and delivery date of polyacrylamide 1285HN in Contract No. 98CIECCO40520.
5.  Statistical table on the procurement of polyacrylamide in 1997 and 1999 issued by the Henan Materials Supply and Marketing Department of China Petroleum & Chemical Corporation. This proved that the unit had purchased polyacrylamide from China International Enterprise Cooperation Corporation and that the sales contract had been fully performed.
6.  China Merchants Bank savings account application form. This proved that the account holder of the China Merchants Bank "All-in-One Card" was Chen Hanshun, the account number was 001007090266, and the account opening date was July 13, 2000.
7.  China Merchants Bank savings deposit slips. This proved that between July 13, 2000, and August 3, 2000, Chen Hanshun deposited USD 81,867 in three installments, all being lump-sum time deposits with a term of two years.
8.  Testimony of the Yayuncun Sub-branch of China Merchants Bank, Beijing. This proved that the password of the aforementioned China Merchants Bank "All-in-One Card" was changed on August 5, 2000.
9.  Text of the safe deposit box rental agreement with the Yayuncun Sub-branch of China Merchants Bank, Beijing. This proved that Cheng Shaozhi rented a safe deposit box at the bank between August 2, 1999, and August 2, 2001.
10. Slip of paper seized by the prosecutorial authority from the bank safe deposit box rented by Cheng Shaozhi, and the appraisal report of the Beijing People's Procuratorate. This proved that the handwriting on the slip was that of Cheng Shaozhi.
11. Testimony of Chen Hanshun. The main content: In July or August 2000, Cheng Shaozhi called Chen Hanshun and said he had been transferred to work in Beijing. Because the several deals Cheng Shaozhi had helped with were quite profitable, to thank him, Chen Hanshun went to China Merchants Bank to open an "All-in-One Card" in his own name and deposited over 80,000 US dollars in three time deposits, each with a two-year term. He drove to the downstairs of Cheng Shaozhi's residence, asked Cheng Shaozhi to get into the car, and gave him the card. He also gave Cheng a slip of paper with the card's password and the deposit amount.
12. Testimony of Cheng Kaiyou, an employee of China International Enterprise Cooperation Corporation. The main content: In June 1997, Chen Hanshun told him that Henan Oilfield had a polyacrylamide business, and Chen was very familiar with the people at Henan Oilfield, hoping that his unit could cooperate with Chen Hanshun to secure this business. During the bidding, China International Enterprise Cooperation Corporation won the bid at a price-to-exchange ratio of 1:10.35. Later, to ensure that he, Chen Hanshun, and China International Enterprise Cooperation Corporation could receive a commission, through Chen Hanshun's efforts, the ratio in the contract was set at 1:10.58, and the domestic trade contract was ultimately signed. The contract was fulfilled by the end of 1998.
13. Testimony of Feng Weimin, Director of the Foreign Affairs Office of Henan Petroleum Exploration Bureau. The main content: He participated in the work of importing polyacrylamide for Henan Petroleum Exploration Bureau in 1998. In 1999, Henan Petroleum Exploration Bureau and China International Enterprise Cooperation Corporation signed an agreement to amend the supply unit price, total price, and delivery date of polyacrylamide 1285HN.
14. Testimony of Wang Jue, former Deputy Director of the Development Department of Henan Petroleum Exploration Bureau. The main content: She participated in the work of importing polyacrylamide for Henan Petroleum Exploration Bureau in 1997 and 1998. Cheng Shaozhi was the head of the bidding team, and China International Enterprise Cooperation Corporation handled the import business.

II. During his tenure as Deputy Director of Henan Petroleum Exploration Bureau and head of the polyacrylamide procurement bidding team, Cheng Shaozhi arranged for Ying Xinhai (separately dealt with), a business person from Shanghai Sanqi Industrial Co., Ltd., to act as the intermediary agent for the business activities between the agent of Japan International Oil Co., Ltd. and Henan Petroleum Exploration Bureau. Ying Xinhai obtained benefits from this. At the end of July 1999, Ying Xinhai made a special trip from Shanghai to Beijing to express gratitude to Cheng Shaozhi for his assistance in the above business activities. After accepting a dinner invitation from Ying Xinhai, Cheng Shaozhi accepted USD 26,000 (equivalent to RMB 215,524.40) given by Ying Xinhai. This money was seized.

Main Evidence to Support the Above Facts:

1.  Relevant agreements signed among Japan International Oil Co., Ltd., Shanghai Sanqi Industrial Co., Ltd., Mitsui Saitec Co., Ltd., and China International Cooperation Company, proving the transaction circumstances.
2.  Certificate issued by Beijing Wuzhou Grand Hotel. This confirmed that Ying Xinhai stayed at the hotel from July 29 to 31, 1999.
3.  Testimony of Ying Xinhai. The main content: He earned USD 60,000 from acting as an agent in the polymer business of Mitsui Company. At the end of July 1999, he brought USD 26,000 to Beijing, invited Cheng Shaozhi to dinner with his cousin Wang Jue, and handed the US dollars to Cheng Shaozhi after dinner.
4.  Testimony of Wang Jue. The main content: When Henan Oilfield purchased polymer from Mitsui Company, Cheng Shaozhi helped her cousin Ying Xinhai become the sales agent for Mitsui Company. After Ying Xinhai signed the agreement with Mitsui Company, he told her that he would not forget Cheng Shaozhi once he made money. In July 1999, Ying Xinhai came to Beijing and invited Cheng Shaozhi to dinner. After dinner, she handed over the over USD 20,000 that Ying Xinhai had brought to Cheng Shaozhi.

Opinion of the Beijing No. 2 Intermediate People's Court:

Article 385, Paragraph 1 of the Criminal Law of the People's Republic of China provides: "Any state functionary who, by taking advantage of his position, extorts property from others, or illegally accepts another person's property and seeks benefits for that person, shall be guilty of the crime of bribery."

The defendant, Cheng Shaozhi, as a state functionary, by taking advantage of his position, sought benefits for others and illegally accepted huge amounts of property. His conduct has constituted the crime of bribery and should be punished according to law. The facts alleged in the indictment regarding the first instance of bribery by Cheng Shaozhi are clear, and the evidence is reliable and sufficient. The argument of Cheng Shaozhi and his defense counsel that the China Merchants Bank "All-in-One Card" was for Chen Hanshun to entrust Cheng Shaozhi to buy stocks lacks evidentiary support. The defense counsel's argument that the "All-in-One Card" was a lump-sum time deposit with a two-year term, and although Cheng Shaozhi changed the bank card's password, he could not withdraw the money, and the ownership of the US dollars stored in the card had not been transferred, therefore the first instance of bribery alleged in the indictment was not established. Upon investigation, the fact that Cheng Shaozhi accepted the China Merchants Bank "All-in-One Card" from Chen Hanshun exists. The testimony of witness Chen Hanshun and the act of Cheng Shaozhi changing the password of the "All-in-One Card" both demonstrate Cheng Shaozhi's intent to accept bribes. Cheng Shaozhi's long-term storage of the bank card in a bank safe deposit box rented by himself conforms to the characteristics of the crime of bribery. As for the argument of Cheng Shaozhi and his defense counsel that Cheng Shaozhi did not accept the US dollars given by Ying Xinhai, upon investigation, the testimonies of both Ying Xinhai and Wang Jue confirm that Cheng Shaozhi, after dining with Ying Xinhai and Wang Jue, accepted the US dollars given by Ying Xinhai. Therefore, Cheng Shaozhi's denial of accepting bribes is not credible.

In summary, the arguments of the defendant Cheng Shaozhi and his defense counsel are all untenable and are not adopted. The figure of USD 32,000 for the second instance of bribery by Cheng Shaozhi alleged in the indictment by the Beijing No. 2 Branch, People's Procuratorate, was inaccurate and should be corrected to the verified figure of USD 26,000 determined during the court investigation.

Accordingly, on December 20, 2002, the Beijing No. 2 Intermediate People's Court rendered the following judgment:

The defendant, Cheng Shaozhi, was found guilty of the crime of bribery and sentenced to 11 years of imprisonment.

After the first-instance judgment was announced, Cheng Shaozhi, dissatisfied, appealed to the Beijing High People's Court.

Cheng Shaozhi's Grounds of Appeal: The determination of the facts in the first instance regarding the first instance of bribery was incorrect in nature. The "All-in-One Card" was given by Chen Hanshun to entrust him to purchase stocks. The determination of the facts in the first instance regarding the second instance of bribery was inconsistent with the facts; he did not accept USD 26,000 from Ying Xinhai.

Defense Counsel's Arguments on Appeal: Cheng Shaozhi did not take advantage of his position to seek benefits for others. The first-instance judgment's finding that Cheng Shaozhi accepting the "All-in-One Card" constituted the crime of bribery was factually unclear and lacked sufficient evidence. The evidence proving that Cheng Shaozhi accepted US dollars from Ying Xinhai was not persuasive.

Opinion of the Beijing High People's Court:

Cheng Shaozhi, as a state functionary, by taking advantage of his position, sought benefits for others and illegally accepted huge amounts of property. His conduct has constituted the crime of bribery and should be punished according to law. Regarding the appeal grounds and defense arguments that "the facts determined in the first instance for the first instance of bribery were incorrect in nature, lacked sufficient evidence, and Cheng Shaozhi did not take advantage of his position to seek benefits for others," upon investigation, the facts that Cheng Shaozhi, as a state functionary, by taking advantage of his position, accepted the "All-in-One Card" given by Chen Hanshun, immediately changed the password, and stored the card in a bank safe deposit box he had rented for a long period until it was seized when the case was uncovered, clearly demonstrate his subjective intention to illegally possess the card and the deposit therein. Although he had not yet actually withdrawn the deposit, his act of accepting the money had already been completed. Therefore, it constituted the crime of bribery. Cheng Shaozhi's claim that the "All-in-One Card" was for Chen Hanshun to entrust him to buy stocks was not supported by any evidence. Regarding the appeal grounds and defense arguments that "the facts determined in the first instance for the second instance of bribery were inconsistent with the facts, Cheng Shaozhi did not accept USD 26,000 from Ying Xinhai, there is now no persuasive evidence to corroborate whether Cheng Shaozhi accepted the US dollars from Ying Xinhai, the witness testimonies are contradictory, and the first-instance judgment applied the law incorrectly," upon investigation, the fact that Cheng Shaozhi illegally accepted USD 26,000 from Ying Xinhai is confirmed not only by the repeated testimonies of witness Ying Xinhai but also by the testimony of witness Wang Jue, who confirmed that she had handed over the bribe money of over USD 20,000 brought by Ying Xinhai to Cheng Shaozhi. Regarding the amount of this bribe, the first-instance court correctly determined it based on relevant evidence. Therefore, the aforementioned appeal grounds and defense arguments of Cheng Shaozhi and his defense counsel lack factual basis and are not adopted.

Accordingly, pursuant to the provisions of Article 189, Item (1) of the Criminal Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, on March 12, 2003, the Beijing High People's Court ruled:

The appeal is dismissed, and the original judgment is affirmed.
